title: Latency vs cost quick tracker (batching + KV cache experiments)
content:
-- Quick experiment log (personal scratch)
-- Aim: surface fast wins for reducing p95 latency without large cost increase.
-- Shortcuts: p50/p95 in ms, cost = estimated $ per 1M tokens for the run config

Variant,Model,SeqLen,BatchSize,KVCache,Prefetch,Bundles(=GPUs),p50_ms,p95_ms,tokens_per_s,cost_per_1M_tokens,notes
baseline,redwood-7b,512,1,off,off,1,48,120,150,45.6,stock single-request latency baseline
l-batch4,redwood-7b,512,4,off,off,1,65,215,520,22.8,throughput up but p95 worse for short tails
kv-on-b1,redwood-7b,512,1,on,off,1,34,85,220,38.0,KV cache warm -> big p95 gains for repeated prefixes
kv-batch2,redwood-7b,512,2,on,off,1,44,110,410,21.0,good tradeoff; some p50 regress vs kv-on-b1 but much higher T/s
quant-int8,redwood-7b-q8,512,1,on,off,1,40,95,240,28.0,slightly slower p50 vs kv-on-b1 but cheaper per token
prefetch-16,redwood-7b,512,1,on,on,1,30,80,260,35.0,prefetch helps p50 and p95 (small batch prewarm)
multi-g2,redwood-7b,512,4,on,on,2,28,70,840,44.0,2 GPUs, good latency and throughput but cost climbs
shortseq-64,redwood-7b,64,1,on,off,1,18,36,600,16.0,short seq shapes are much cheaper — consider routing small queries to short model variant

-- Observations / quick takeaways:
- KV cache warmups are the easiest win for p95 on repeated/prefix-heavy workloads (chat sessions). If >40% requests are continuation, enable KV aggressively.
- Small batching (2) with KV on often gives best throughput/cost balance for mixed workloads; batch=4 helps throughput but drags p95 for single-shot low-latency paths.
- Prefetch (prewarming sequence kernels for common prompt lengths) reduces p50 by ~10-20% in these quick runs — promising to combine with KV.
- Quantization (int8) helps cost but watch p50 spike for some prompts — test with eval set.
- Routing: consider a lightweight front-door rule: seq_len < 96 -> shortseq variant; session_continuation -> KV-enabled path.

-- Next steps / TODOs:
- Run controlled eval on 1k real user prompts comparing baseline, kv-on-b1, kv-batch2, quant-int8 (linear jobs). Add p99 for production decision. (Owner: Priya)
- Add a synthetic tail test (no cache warm) to measure worst-case p95 for batch=2/4. (Owner: Marco)
- Benchmark warmup patterns: prefetch disabled/enabled x varying prompt lengths. (Owner: Sana)
- Add cost per 1M tokens to the per-route billing spreadsheet and surface in Console suggestions. (cross-team)

-- Quick commands I used (notes):
# run single-shot microbench: python infra/bench/run_infer.py --model redwood-7b --seq 512 --batch 1 --kv off --runs 200
# enable kv warm path: python infra/bench/run_infer.py --model redwood-7b --seq 512 --batch 1 --kv on --warm 50 --runs 200
# multi-gpu stress: infra/bench/run_multi_gpu.sh redwood-7b 4 2 --prefetch

-- Questions / unknowns (notes to self):
- How stable are these numbers across instance families (A100 vs H100)? need spot-checks.
- Does the cost model used here reflect preemption and amortized infra? probably optimistic; verify with infra finance.
